problems.where: docs/VERIFY.md:520 (title and the fixture sentence); docs/VERIFY.md:521 (last sentence)
problems.text:
Two statements in row 520 are not true of the final tree.

- "passed all twelve with the final binaries": only five of the twelve fixtures were run after the noise limit was taken out, as the second refix report says itself. The other seven (go-buffer-pool, go-ticker-modern, node-price-board-flat, rust-tree-parent-links-weak, rust-batch-buffers, native-arena-reuse, jvm-order-cache-bounded) last ran on binaries that still had the limit. Row 521 repeats "passed all twelve".
- The title still says the purge test read "the scatter of a flat column" as retained, with status `corrected`. The body of the same row says that limit was tried and left out, and that the case is open.

Direction: drop "or the scatter of a flat column" from the title. Write the fixture sentence from the final full dynamic run, or say now which five ran on the final tree. The three fixtures I ran on the final tree pass.

The leak-side test pins only the exact limit that was removed. Its growth is 80,000 against 3 noise units of about 80,070.

Replayed on the test's own series:
- With the 3-unit limit put back it reads `no-growth` and non-leak, so the test fails, as the report says.
- With a limit of 2.9 noise units it still reads retained and inconclusive, so the test passes.

The second half of the test (a 2 MB step) reads retained in every variant, HEAD included. Direction: put the growth just above the minimum (about 40 KB under the same scatter), so that any scatter-scaled limit fails the test.

Inexact statements about the open case and the command-level test.

- "a flat Python run whose `os.rss` passes the first trend": os.rss votes whenever any column of memory in use passed the first trend (crates/dla-cli/src/alloc/pick.rs:375-379), not only when it passed itself. In my python-report-memo-bounded run only py.traced_peak and py.traced.pre_gc passed, and both unbound alloc-tests read inconclusive through os.rss (growth 176.1 and 73.7 KB, drop 12.3 KB). The earlier acceptance run read the same.
- "That test does not reach the retained path" (row 521 and the test comment): in 1 of my 8 command-level runs os.rss_file read purge retained (growth 77.8 KB, drop 0) and read non-leak through the exemption. So the test does exercise the exemption in some runs, and would fail there without it.
- "4 of 8 here" (both rows): 1 of 8 read inconclusive in my runs.
- Wording: "the floor" remains in both rows though the floor is gone. Row 521 now carries a measured size ("about 160 KB"), against the brief's rule of no byte counts. alloc_test.rs:353 is 101 characters long.

Open by the refix's decision: a flat Python run can still read inconclusive through os.rss, and the command-level test does not assert the overall verdict the brief asked for. The decision is one of the two the last check offered, and both rows say it.

Data from 8 runs of the scenario with the tree binary:
- 7 read non-leak and 1 inconclusive (os.rss growth 155.6 KB, drop 12.3 KB).
- os.rss_anon at the warm-up point stood below every later point in all 8 runs, by 45 to 246 KB. os.rss_file at that point mostly stood above the later points.
- The trim now returns about 12 KB, so two runs with growth of 41 and 53 KB read partial, not retained.

No action unless the owner wants the reference of the purge growth changed.

Readings on prepared series that follow from the brief's rule as written. No action.

- A slow real leak reads non-leak where HEAD read inconclusive, when its two single readings happen to differ by 32 KiB or less: 6 of 200 seeds (Python, 8 KB per point under a 60 KB scatter) and 4 of 200 (native, 30 KB per point, 8+8 points). With the removed limit these were 79 and 119.
- In 5 of 200 seeds of the Python shape leak becomes inconclusive. The flat os.rss_file now reads non-leak beside the leaking os.rss, and `overall` (unchanged) calls leak beside non-leak inconclusive.
- A Go heap growth of 17,000 or 32,768 B and an os.rss_anon step of 30 KB, each kept by the purge, move from inconclusive to non-leak. 34,000 B and 68 KB stay inconclusive.

confirmed:
The second refix does what the second check asked on every item, and the tests and my three fixtures pass. One problem remains: two statements in VERIFY row 520 are not true of the final tree. Two minor items remain: a thin leak-side test and inexact wording.

**Items of the second check**
- Problem 1 (noise limit): fixed by taking it out.
  - `judge::purge_floor` is gone and `test_column` passes `min_rise` (alloc_cmd.rs:250-262).
  - The code path extracted from the tree is identical to the earlier check's "minimum only" variant.
- Problem 2 (flat Python run inconclusive through os.rss): accepted as open, and both rows say so. Data is in the first note.
- Minor 3 (`platform` import between the readings): fixed. In 12 bare runs per agent:
  - Tree agent: `before` equals the checkpoint's reading; `after` is 57 KB below `before` for os.rss and equal for os.rss_file. The tightened test passes 12 of 12.
  - First-refix agent: `after` is 98 to 111 KB above `before`. The test fails 12 of 12.
  - HEAD agent: `before` is 1.65 to 1.74 MB above the own reading. The test fails 12 of 12.
- Minor 4 (test comment): rewritten. One sentence in it is inexact (second minor).
- Minor 5 (overlong lines): fixed. No added line in the reference or the README is over 100 characters.

**Items of the first check**
- File-backed leak could read non-leak: still fixed. os.rss_file votes; only its purge reading is dropped, and only when its plateau reads plateau.
- Python trim read `before` after its import: still fixed in the harness.
- False VERIFY sentence: still gone.

**Claims of the second refix report**
- Confirmed:
  - `combine` and `overall` have no changed line.
  - Leak-side test seen failing: with the limit back its series reads `no-growth` and non-leak.
  - The two floor tests are removed; neither existed at HEAD.
  - Rows 520 and 521 have 4 cells each and no plan or model names.
  - pick.rs is unchanged by this pass.
- False: row 520's "passed all twelve with the final binaries" (the report itself says seven were not rerun).
- Different here: "4 of 8" inconclusive; I got 1 of 8.

**Decisions and tests**
- The purge test uses the plateau minimum and nothing else: yes. `judge::combine` unchanged: yes.
- No test was skipped, ignored or weakened against HEAD. The diff removes no assertion; the existing purge tests only gained the 0.0 argument.

**Runs here**
- `cargo test -j 2 --no-fail-fast -p dla-cli --test alloc_test`: 4 passed.
- Unit tests of the alloc code (`--bin dla alloc`): 76 passed.
- `cargo test -j 2 -p dla-workload --test harness_capture_python`: 16 passed, both new tests among them.
- Workspace clippy and the Windows-gnu clippy with `-D warnings`: exit 0, both from cache. `cargo fmt --all --check` clean. `dla schema --check` ok.

**Adversarial cases (HEAD against tree, prepared series)**
1. File-backed leak below the noise of os.rss: identical to HEAD in all 800 seeded series. None reads non-leak. The first refix's shift from leak to inconclusive is gone.
2. Flat Python run with the trim purge:
   - New agent's record: non-leak. Old agent's record: still inconclusive.
   - 100 KB of early growth under a 60 KB scatter: inconclusive, as at HEAD.
   - 200 flat seeds: inconclusive in 158 at HEAD, 39 now.
3. Go heap leak of 100 KB with a retained purge: identical to HEAD in all 1,400 seeded series. The column reads leak in 200 of 200 with a 6 KB scatter. None reads non-leak. 126 scatter-free steps: none changed.

A case that read leak or inconclusive for a good reason and now reads non-leak: only through the brief's own 32 KiB rule, in 6 and 4 of 200 seeds of two slow-leak shapes (second note). No such move in cases 1 and 3.

**Fixtures** (copies of binaries built from this tree, `--parallel 1`; all three pass)

| Fixture | Now (refuted, confirmed, rule-out, leaks, passed columns) | Earlier run |
|---|---|---|
| python-report-memo-bounded | 1, 0, true, 0, 2 | 1, 0, true, 0, 2 |
| python-graph-churn | 2, 0, true, 0, 8 | 0, 0, false, 0, 3 (failed) |
| go-gc-tuned-batch | 3, 0, true, 0, 1 | 3, 0, true, 0, 2 |

What the unbound alloc-tests read:
- python-report-memo-bounded: both inconclusive through os.rss (plateau, purge retained), as in the earlier run. The fixture passes through its bound probe test.
- python-graph-churn: both non-leak. os.rss and os.rss_anon read plateau with purge released (growth 3.8 MB, drop 9.4 MB). os.rss_file did not pass the first trend.
- go-gc-tuned-batch: both non-leak. go.released passed the first trend and reads plateau with purge `no-growth`; os.rss reads plateau with purge released. go.heap_objects did not pass the first trend.

Machine time of my runs: about 27 minutes. Evidence is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dla/f6814273-1d53-58fc-a01a-0b3a3a3915ac/scratchpad/u9chk-N1b/r2/`: `replay-tests.txt`, `replay-sweep.txt`, `replay.txt`, `replay-leak-moves.txt`, `cmdlevel-summary.txt`, `cmdlevel-series.txt`, `dyn-summary.txt`, `py/trim-summary.txt`. The replay source is in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-dla/f6814273-1d53-58fc-a01a-0b3a3a3915ac/scratchpad/u9chk-N1b/replay/`.

- Both clippy runs returned from cache. `python3 bench/runner/test_grade.py` was not run; no file of this package is read by it.
- The os.rss_file exemption and the go.heap_objects `no-growth` path on a fixture run: neither column passed the first trend in my runs. The exemption did show in one command-level run.
- That the JVM purge steps move os.rss_file: by reading only, from the earlier checks.
- The sweep rates come from prepared series with uniform scatter. The rates on real programs are unknown.
- The skip of the Linux-only tests on macOS and Windows, and how often the chance events recur on the runners.
